question: Should OpenClaw accept static `sandbox.docker.env` SecretRefs when the resolved values still become Docker container environment variables visible through Docker/container metadata?
rationale: The implementation shape is bounded, but the durable choice is a security/product boundary about whether SecretRef-backed credentials are appropriate for Docker env delivery.

options.title: Accept Docker env SecretRefs
options.body: Land or sponsor the linked PR after recording that the existing Docker metadata-exposure warning is acceptable for SecretRef-backed env values.

options.title: Require a stronger warning first
options.body: Ask the linked PR to explicitly name SecretRef-backed Docker env metadata exposure in public docs before landing.

options.title: Reject env-based delivery
options.body: Close or pause the linked PR and route secret delivery toward a non-env or per-call design such as https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/80329.

recommendation.title: Accept Docker env SecretRefs
recommendation.body: Land or sponsor the linked PR after recording that the existing Docker metadata-exposure warning is acceptable for SecretRef-backed env values.

likelyOwner.reason: Josh has the strongest merged history across both SecretRef credential surfaces and explicit Docker sandbox env propagation.
